findings.text: Generic thread flags number the first five positions from zero upward. TIF_NOTIFY_RESUME is 0 for work on return to user mode, TIF_SIGPENDING is 1 for a pending signal, TIF_NOTIFY_SIGNAL is 2 for available signal notifications, TIF_MEMDIE is 3 for termination under memory pressure handling, and TIF_NEED_RESCHED is 4 for a reschedule request.

Numbering continues with TIF_NEED_RESCHED_LAZY at 5 for a deferred reschedule, TIF_POLLING_NRFLAG at 6 for idle polling state, TIF_USER_RETURN_NOTIFY at 7 for user return notification, TIF_UPROBE at 8 for probe breakpoint or single step, TIF_PATCH_PENDING at 9 for pending live update, and TIF_RESTORE_SIGMASK at 10 for signal mask restoration.

The upper generic positions place TIF_RSEQ at 11 for restartable sequence handling and TIF_HRTIMER_REARM at 12 for timer rearm handling. Each companion _TIF mask name denotes a single bit selected by its index, so one flag can be tested or set without affecting others.
The generic cycle counter type cycles_t is an unsigned machine word, wide enough to hold a raw timer value on the target.
A generic inline accessor get_cycles supplies a cycle count and yields constant zero when no architecture implementation exists, giving a portable fallback.

Generic topology offers query operations cpu_to_node and cpu_to_mem plus cpumask_of_node and pcibus_to_node with cpumask_of_pcibus, together with setter operations set_numa_node and set_cpu_numa_node plus set_numa_mem and set_cpu_numa_mem for node association.

Defaults describe a single node system without NUMA. CPU to node or memory answers 0 while ignoring its input, node mask answers the online CPU set, bus to node answers missing with negative one, bus mask falls back to all CPUs when missing and otherwise uses the node mask, and all setters discard their arguments.

Generic virtual system call support exposes accessors __arch_get_vdso_u_time_data and __arch_get_vdso_u_rng_data returning pointers to shared user visible time data and random number data held in global objects.
Generic hooks __arch_update_vdso_clock and __arch_sync_vdso_time_data accept a clock or data pointer and perform no action, leaving all work to architecture code when needed.

Framebuffer support provides pgprot_framebuffer to adjust page protection toward write combining for the mapping, and video_is_primary_device as a primary device test that always reports not primary under the generic definition.

Sized framebuffer loads fb_readb and fb_readw plus fb_readl and fb_readq, and stores fb_writeb and fb_writew plus fb_writel and fb_writeq, delegate to the corresponding raw input output primitives for one, two, four and eight byte widths.

Block framebuffer transfers fb_memcpy_fromio and fb_memcpy_toio copy between normal memory and input output memory in either direction, and fb_memset_io fills input output memory with a byte value, delegating to generic memory input output helpers, with fb_memset as a short alias for the fill operation.

The default load bias LOAD_OFFSET is 0 and the generic structure alignment STRUCT_ALIGNMENT is 32 bytes, with helpers ALIGN_FUNCTION and STRUCT_ALIGN to advance the location counter to function or structure boundaries.

Generic linker definitions group executable and data input sections by name families. TEXT_MAIN collects main text plus many prefixed text variants while excluding certain startup and exit spellings, and DATA_MAIN with SDATA_MAIN and RODATA_MAIN plus BSS_MAIN and SBSS_MAIN collect plain, small, read only, zero initialized and small zero initialized families including compiler generated suffixes.

SCHED_DATA orders scheduler class entries from highest to lowest priority between two symbols marking the ends. INIT_TASK_DATA reserves a thread sized region for initial task and stack with start and end markers. JUMP_TABLE_DATA and STATIC_CALL_DATA emit bounded ranges, and RO_AFTER_INIT_DATA brackets read only after init data with alignment and markers.

DATA_DATA aggregates executable, writable, reference, shared aligned, unlikely, once, tracepoint, dynamic debug, code tag, profiling and tracing inputs. NOSAVE_DATA with CACHE_HOT_DATA and PAGE_ALIGNED_DATA plus READ_MOSTLY_DATA and CACHELINE_ALIGNED_DATA, and KERNEL_DTB, each use aligned bounded ranges with markers. RO_DATA collects read only data, scheduler data, after init data, tracepoint tables, PCI fixup phases, symbol and parameter tables, exception, notes and type information between start and end markers.

BOUNDED_SECTION and HEADERED_SECTION helpers define paired start and stop symbols around kept inputs, with variants for label placement and for link once headers. Device tree tables such as TIMER_OF_TABLES and IRQCHIP_OF_MATCH_TABLE plus CLK_OF_TABLES and related OF_TABLE forms, with ACPI_PROBE_TABLE and THERMAL_TABLE plus LSM_TABLE and EARLY_LSM_TABLE and EARLYCON_TABLE, emit aligned bounded tables only when their configuration is enabled and otherwise expand to nothing.

Tracing, profiling, live patch, kprobe, error injection, system call metadata, raw tracepoint, print format and branch annotation inputs use MCOUNT_REC and FTRACE_STUB_HACK plus KEEP_PATCHABLE and LIKELY_PROFILE with BRANCH_PROFILE and KPROBE_BLACKLIST plus ERROR_INJECT_WHITELIST and FTRACE_EVENTS with TRACE_PRINTKS and TRACEPOINT_STR plus TRACE_SYSCALLS and BPF_RAW_TP. Each emits an aligned bounded table when enabled and nothing otherwise, as do NOTES_HEADERS with NOTES_HEADERS_RESTORE and RO_EXCEPTION_TABLE plus KCFI_TRAPS and NOINSTR_TEXT with TEXT_SPLIT and TEXT_UNLIKELY plus TEXT_HOT.

Empty generic headers timex and topology plus trace_clock and unwind_user with user and vsyscall and video define only their include guards. The trace clock header additionally defines ARCH_TRACE_CLOCKS with no value, signalling that no extra clocks are required.

Several generics are intentionally degenerate and only safe as fallbacks. get_cycles yields zero, topology pretends a single node, bus NUMA lookup reports missing, video primary detection reports false, and virtual clock maintenance does nothing, so architectures needing real behaviour must provide their own definitions.
